title: COMPRENAD – a prospective, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled nutritional intervention study to compare precursors for NAD+ production
summary:
Vitamin B3 is an essential nutrient that comes in two forms: nicotinamide and nicotinic acid. Despite their names, these compounds are unrelated to the nicotine found in tobacco or e-cigarettes. The body rather uses them, or the protein building block tryptophan, to produce nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+). Another nutrient that can be taken to support NAD+ production is nicotinamide riboside (NR). 

NAD+ plays a central role in energy metabolism, cell repair and immune defence. NAD+ currently receives attention because many dietary supplements aim to boost NAD+ levels in the body. This is intended to promote healthy ageing and longevity. Recent research shows that the gut microbiome, which is the community of microorganisms (mainly bacteria) living in the gut, is important for NAD+ metabolism. Most of these microorganisms live in the lower part of the small intestine and in the large intestine. Some NAD+ precursors such as NR can be converted by gut bacteria into forms the body can use more easily. However, it is unclear which vitamin B3 nutritional products are optimal for supporting NAD+ metabolism and how the gut microbiome can best be used for this purpose. 

The University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein has developed two new tablets: CICR-NAM and CIR-NA. These tablets release nicotinamide (CICR-NAM) or nicotinic acid (CIR-NA) directly to the gut microbiome. Conventional tablets, by contrast, release vitamin B3 mainly in the upper small intestine. Therefore, it hardly reaches the gut microbiome. The site of release is the only significant difference between CICR-NAM/CIR-NA and conventional products. 

The COMPRENAD nutritional intervention study will be the first to compare CICR-NAM (at two different doses), CIR-NA and NR in healthy adults. It will measure how these products affect NAD+ production. The study will also examine NAD+ metabolism, the gut microbiome and gene activity in blood cells.

interventions.name: CICR-NAM (controlled-ileocolonic-release nicotinamide), 1 film-coated tablet (500 mg nictoinamide) once daily.
CICR-NAM, 2 film-coated tablets (2 x 500 mg nicotinamide) once daily.
NR (nicotinamide riboside): 4 capsules (4 x 300 mg NR) once daily.
CIR-NA (controlled-ileal-release nicotinic acid), 1 film-coated tablet (1 x 100 mg nicotinic acid) once daily.
CICR-NAM placebo, 1 film-coated tablet once daily.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Able to understand and to sign a written informed consent prior to study enrollment
Exclusion criteria:
• Known history of allergy or intolerance to components of the investigational products.
• Any chronic medical condition and/or history of significant medical condition (e.g., malig nancy, gastrointestinal or metabolic disease, chronic inflammatory condition, uncontrolled diabetes, or cardiovascular diseases) and/or psychiatric condition (e.g., depression, psychotic disorders, or chronic insomnia), which in the opinion of the Investigator may risk participant wellbeing/safety, impede participant compliance with study procedures or ability to com plete the study, and/or could confound the results of the study.
• Any acute illness or any recent medical intervention including vaccination within 14 days before the first dose of investigational product.
• Female participants who are pregnant or intending to become pregnant, lactating, and/or breastfeeding.
• Women of childbearing potential who are not currently using medically effective forms of contraception. Medically effective forms of contraception include hormonal methods, such as the contraceptive pill or implant (stable use for at least 3 months), an intrauterine device in use at least 30 days prior to enrolment, or barrier methods such as diaphragm or condom, in use at least 14 days prior to enrolment. 
• Use of supplements containing more than 20 mg per daily dose of NAD+ or any NAD+ precur sor (e.g., NAM, NA or NR) or L-tryptophan up to 30 days before the first dose of investigational product.
• The use of prescription drugs known to potentially interact with NAD+ precursors (e.g., tetra cycline antibiotics, anticoagulants, or bile acid sequestrants) within 14 days or five half-lives (whichever is longer) before the first dose of investigational product. 
• Higher doses of proton pump inhibitors, targeted H2-receptor antagonists or antacid formu lations (i.e., doses equivalent to > 40 mg pantoprazole per day). 
• On a self-restricted diet, controlled diet, or special therapeutic diet (e.g., low carbohydrate diet, ketogenic diet, or intermittent fasting) up to 30 days before first dose of investigational product.
• Currently participating in another research study or clinical trial.
• Any other circumstances or medical conditions which could contradict a study participation and lead the Investigator to assess the participant as not eligible.
